News.title: Watch: Japan fans celebrate on street crossing – but only while lights are green
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the opening Group F match between Japan and Netherlands from Dallas. Netherlands, the Oranje or Hup Holland Hup in old money, have an enviable group stage record at World Cups when they make it and have not lost at this stage in 16 matches stretching back to 1994 when they were beaten by Belgium, of all people, in Orlando’s stifling humidity.

Ronnie Koeman, their captain 32 years ago, is back in charge for the second time having initially jumped ship for the poisoned chalice of managing Barcelona at the height of their financial crisis, returning in time to take them to Euro 2024 where, after a rotten start when they scraped through the group in third place, they went on to hammer Romania, dispatch Turkey in the quarters and lost the semi only in the 90th minute when Ollie Watkins came off the bench for England and laced in the winner. But they were pretty ropey in qualification yet their two draws with Poland did not bite them and no none-winner, when they qualify, has a better record of going deep: three runners-up spots, two further semi-finals and a couple of quarter-finals.

Japan, by contrast, who made the last 16 at the last two World Cups have never gone beyond that round. In 2022 they were eliminated on penalties by Croatia after the Blue Samurai had thrilling beaten Germany and Spain in the group of death. After a disappointing Asia Cup when they were knocked out by Iran in the quarter-finals, they stormed through qualifying, scoring 54 goals, and have won six friendlies on the bounce including victories over Scotland at Hampden and England at Wembley.

Both squads have been weakened by injury. Japan have lost their captain Wataru Endo having previously had to leave Takumi Minamino and Kaoru Mitoma at home while the Oranje are without regulars Jurrien Timber, Matthijs de Ligt, Jerdy Schouten and Xavi Simons.

News.title: Royal Ascot 2026 tips: Ante-post selections by our expert
News.content:
Day one: Tuesday June 16

2.30 Queen Anne Stakes

The meeting opens with a bang and the first Group One race of the week over Ascot’s stiff straight mile. Occasionally you get a funny result and the winners of the main trial, the Lockinge Stakes at Newbury – last month it was won by this race’s favourite Notable Speech – only have a so-so record in the race. This year, you would think this race is Notable Speech’s to lose. Few milers have his turn of foot at the finish but Charlie Appleby’s horses are hardly coming into the meeting on fire. His strike rate is not bad but he has not been running many. His second string, Opera Ballo, put himself in line for a crack at this when beating Field of Gold by three lengths at Sandown in April. He won a Group One at Meydan in the winter, but this is a step up in class. No horse likes Ascot more than Docklands though. He won the Britannia, was second in this race in 2024 then won it last year. More Thunder should be closer to Notable Speech than he was at Newbury.

Charlie Brooks’s tip: Zeus Olympics

Marlborough’s tip: Opera Ballo

3.05 Coventry Stakes

Continuing with the theme that the best racing of the whole week is day one, this six-furlong Group Two race is the most prestigious two-year-old race of the week. Aidan O’Brien, who has won it 11 times, will have the likely favourite in either Great Barrier Reef – winner of both his starts including a Group Three last time – or Confucius – a good winner of his maiden last time – depending on which Ryan Moore selects. At a working man’s price I like Richard Hannon’s Cut A Dash, a good winner over five furlongs at York on debut in May, with the promise of more to come over a longer distance. As the father of two flame-haired daughters, I will put the family fiver will be on the 50-1 shot The Ginger Kid.

Charlie Brooks’s tip: Great Barrier Reef

Marlborough’s tip: Royal Heritage

3.40 King Charles III Stakes

Still known in many quarters as the King’s Stand Stakes but renamed in honour of the King, this five-furlong Group One sprint is for the quickest horses at Ascot. The received wisdom is that a medium Aussie sprinter is still better than anything Europe has to offer, so Overpass is likely to start favourite but it has been a while between drinks for him. Last year’s winner, Jim Goldie’s American Affair, did not run again in 2025, but his two runs this year, including a much-improved second in the Temple Stakes, will have put him spot on for a repeat. Others to look out for include Night Raider, who is much improved for the snip, and the flying French filly Rayevka.

Charlie Brooks’s tip: Overpass

Marlborough’s tip: Cover Up

4.20 St James’s Palace Stakes

The Group One mile for three-year-old colts, on the round course, has attracted the English and Irish Guineas winners and anything else which missed the boat on the early Classics. That it has done with, respectively, Bow Echo, Gstaad, and Talk of New York. In trying to turn the Newmarket tables on Bow Echo, Gstaad will have a pacemaker but George Boughey’s colt should still be too good and the small field should mean not too much traffic from his inside draw but Gstaad is in the same boat there.

Charlie Brooks’s tip: Bow Echo

Marlborough’s tip: Bow Echo

5.00 Ascot Stakes

While most Flat trainers go for a cup of tea at this stage, their jump counterparts get one of their moments of the week in the two and a half mile handicap which is nearly always won by a predominantly jump trainer. The King and Queen have Reaching High in this. He represents one of the best chances of a Royal winner this week. He has not run since finishing a close up ninth in this last year when he met bad traffic problems and runs off the same mark. The lack of run would normally be a worry but I think its safe to say Mullins will have him fit as a fiddle. All he needs is a bit of luck.

Charlie Brooks’s tip: Small Fry

Marlborough’s tip: Tim Toe

5.35 Wolferton Stakes

A mile-and-a-quarter Listed race for horses which have not won a Group One or Two since last August. The King and Queen might have recent York winner Warrant Holder in this. It was won by Richard Hannon’s Haatem last year and he is back for another go in the Wathnan silks, which, in a short space of time, have made this meeting its raison d’être – if in doubt in any race this week go for one of theirs.

Charlie Brooks’s tip: Nahraan

Marlborough’s tip: Royal Rhyme

6.10 Copper Horse Stakes

Another long distance handicap for those with a touch of the slows but Valiancy, owned by Ascot specialist Wathnan, did not look short of toe at Hamilton on his first start of the season when quickening smartly after being hemmed in to win a bit smugly in the end. Really getting his act together now and stays the trip but with gears which should make him hard to beat here.

Charlie Brooks’s tip: Too Soon

Marlborough’s tip: Valiancy

Day two: Wednesday June 17

2.30 Queen Mary Stakes.

A Group Two for rattling quick juvenile fillies over five furlongs. This looks quite international and there are a few here who are not coming for the Ascot air. Morley is a name closely associated with British racing and Tom Morley, a Briton who forged his own way in New York, has a bit of what they call “black type” in his pedigree including uncle David who won the Gold Cup with Celleric and jump trainer Henry Daly. His More Champagne won on debut in the US by over six lengths from one of Wesley Ward’s so she must be fast. Drazinda, a first Aga Khan Studs two-year-old to run at Ascot in a long time, comes from France but from the home team I like Crystal Queen who travelled very well to win the Hilary Needler at Beverley and is clearly suited by a stiff five furlongs.

3.05 Queen’s Vase

A mile and three quarters for three-year-olds making it something of a St Leger trial. The King and Queen could go with Point of Law in this. It may come a little soon in his career and it would be quite a big step up in trip but that applies to quite a few of these including Causeway, Aidan O’Brien’s colt who is three from three this season. Limestone has won his last three for Joseph O’Brien and is sure to get the trip having already won over a mile and five but I liked the way Andrew Balding’s Galiyan won at Chester. The further he went the better he went.

3.40 Duke of Cambridge Stakes

A Group Two over a mile for four-year-old plus fillies. Fallen Angel is probably the best horse in this race having won at least one Group One every season of her career but she is yet to win at Ascot - third in this last year - and it may be worth taking a punt on Friendly Soul. She was still travelling well first time out at Haydock when she was the unlucky one to put her foot in a hole. That was probably not the ideal preparation but you can put a line through the fact that she was pulled up after that.

4.20 Prince of Wales’s Stakes

A Group One mile and a quarter race for four-year-olds plus and is, unquestionably, highlight of day two. This pits two of the best in the world, the Arc winner Daryz and Ombudsman, last year’s winner of this race, against each other with a strong supporting cast of Group One winners including Almaqam, who is finally realising his latent potential, and the fillies Kalpana, See The Fire and Minnie Hauk. Ironically before the Arc it was “would Daryz stay?” Now he has won it, the same people are asking “is he quick enough for 10 furlongs?” He has already added two Group One notches to his four-poster this season over nine and 10 furlongs. He’s quick enough alright.

5.00 Royal Hunt Cup

If day one’s handicaps are not up to much, this is one of the meeting’s marquee handicap events. It is over the straight mile. There are a few old friends in here and things to take into consideration like the market and the draw but Linwood makes appeal at this stage. He is young, improving, won well on his reappearance and it looks like there’s more to come from Richard Hannon’s four-year-old. Owner Jim Hay seldom leaves the meeting without a winner.

5.30 Kensington Palace Handicap

A handicap for four-year-old plus fillies and mares over a mile. For a four-year-old the William Haggas trained Alobayyah is very lightly raced having only had four starts but they clearly think something of her. She ran an eye-catching third over a mile at Ascot in May staying on strongly off a slow pace. It would be a surprise if they went so slowly at a Festival where jockeys tend to get a bit more excitable.

5.35 Windsor Castle Stakes

A six furlong Listed race for two-year-olds whose sire won over a distance in excess of six and a half furlongs at two or seven and a half furlongs at three. The King and Queen could go with King’s Prize in this and the way she won at Nottingham in debut, she might be one of their better chances this week. This looks a better race than the Queen Mary for Victorious (if Aidan needs any race planning advice, I’m available) because of the trip and it might be a bit easier. As always in these two-year-old races there are plenty of unknown quantities who have run and won just the once. King’s Prize, Moonrise and Sale Shark fit that bill but I like Controlla to get Amo racing on the scoresheet. She was just pipped by Victorious on her only start and can not only improve but reverse that form.

Day three: Thursday June 18

2.30 Chesham Stakes

At seven furlongs this is the longest contest for two-year-olds at Ascot this week. Aix La Chapelle looks the Aidan O’Brien No 1 in this. He made up a good bit of ground late on and finished strongly to win a Curragh maiden earlier this month. I was quite impressed by Revels – no surprise at that name as he’s owned by the Mars family – on his debut at Redcar in may. He won by three lengths. With his big white face you won’t miss this chestnut colt coming up Ascot’s straight.

3.05 King George V Stakes

A mile-and-a-half handicap for three-year-olds rated up to 105. Lost Boys, trained by David Menuisier in Sussex, will be one of the favourites for this race on the back of his London Gold Cup win over a mile and a quarter at Newbury. He has subsequently been bought by Wathnan who has a pretty good strike rate for buying ready-made Ascot winners. He beat Sahara King by a head that day and as Wathnan own that horse you would imagine it knows what it is doing. The extra quarter of a mile should be fine for him.

3.40 Ribblesdale Stakes

A mile-and-a-half Group Two for fillies making it something of an Oaks consolation for those that needed a couple of extra weeks. The King and Queen could have a go with Golden Orbit in this, but she would need to take a bit big step forward on her first start of the season. If Legacy Link runs just 13 days after finishing second in the Oaks, a race in which she had no answers to Thundering On, she sets the standard. That’s not usually the Gosdens’ or Juddmonte’s modus operandi so she would have to be in cracking form to go. Earth Shot, who was just beaten at Goodwood last time over a mile and a quarter, might be the one stepping up in trip.

4.15 Gold Cup

A marathon trip of two-and-a-half miles first run in 1807, a year best known here for the abolition of slavery while in Europe Napoleon was smacking the Russians. Last year’s winner Trawlerman is back, but without a prep and an eye condition which makes him sensitive to light. However, if he’s on song he will be hard to beat. The obvious two young pretenders are last year’s St Leger first and second – Scandinavia and Rahiebb. At a better price is Carmers who is bidding to emulate the late Queen’s Estimate who took the Queen’s Vase here in 2013, before winning the Gold Cup a year later. Keeping them all honest will be Sweet William, who is always consistent in these races.

4.50 Britannia Stakes

A mile for three-year-old colts rated up to 105. We’re Goosers looks a good honest sort. He galloped his rivals into submission winning by a wide margin and finishing strong through the line at Newmarket last time. He gets a mile but seven furlongs may be his optimum. St Anton won over a mile at Carlisle so this mile might not be quite stiff enough for him, but he is in with a shout, while Laureate Crown is another from the same stable as We’re Goosers.

5.35 Hampton Court Stakes

A Group Three mile-and-a-quarter race for three-year-olds who have not won a Group One or Two. A few horses in here have had their sights lowered after so-so efforts in the Derby, but most of those would have had a hard enough race in the conditions so fresher legs may be the answer. William Haggas was very disappointed with Morshdi after the Dante at York last month. If he can put a line through that poor run so must we. Causeway is likely to start favourite, but for those who like a double-figure pride Mountain Cat could outrun his odds.

6.10 Buckingham Palace Stakes

A seven-furlong handicap to finish off Ladies’ Day. I’ll have to come back to you nearer the time for this race but Arctic Dawn, trained by Dan and Clare Kubler, looks progressive despite being a five-year-old and a win a for a smaller set up might not go amiss at this stage.

Day four: Friday June 19

2.30 Albany Stakes

Six furlong contest for fillies. Aidan O’Brien’s Sun Goddess is likely to be a warm order for this after a six lengths demolition of her opposition at The Curragh on her second start. It is hard to pick holes in that performance and it is hard to oppose her. That said there will be plenty of once run once won could be anythings in the race. Karl Burke’s Wild Blossom, a £300k breeze-up filly for Wathnan, won over five furlongs at Carlisle by 10 lengths. She has the Queen Mary option but Venetian Sun, who won that maiden for the stable last year, went on to win the Albany.

3.05 Commonwealth Cup

A six furlong Group One sprint for speedy three-year-olds. Ascot’s stiff six may be just what Albert Einstein needs but for me he has been a bit disappointing. If you fancy him you should also fancy Song of The Clyde who beat him at Newbury and will be three times the odds. Clive Cox also has the quick Coppul in this. Venetian Sun, last year’s Albany winner, will probably start favourite on the back of her Sandy Lane three length success but it might be worth taking a punt on Amo’s Wesley Ward trained Outfielder who has looked blisteringly quick on his first two starts in the US this year. Each-way 50-1 shot Spicy Marg will enjoy being back on the quick ground again.

3.40 Duke of Edinburgh Stakes

Mile and a half handicap for three-year-old plus. I suspect a few have been laid out for this race but Yabher looked much improved at four when he won on his reappearance for William Haggas at Goodwood by six lengths. Even winning so far I am not sure he laid all his cards on the table for the handicapper and despite a rise in the handicap he should go close here.

4.20 Coronation Stakes

A mile on the round course for three-year-old fillies, the St James’s Palace for the ladies as it were. After running down the field in the Guineas at Newmarket Precise looked rocket-propelled, reversing the form with stable companion True Love, in the Irish equivalent. Anything like a reproduction of that would make her hard to beat. Anything Wathnan buys should be given consideration at the fact that it has come in for The Prettiest Star is a bit of tip in itself. She had Precise behind her when fourth in the Guineas and the new owner has clearly seen something.

5.00 Sandringham Stakes

A mile handicap for three-year-old fillies. Symbol of Majesty had no sort of a run at Wolverhampton on her third start after winning on turf first time out this season but that probably did not do her handicap too much harm and this is an easier option than the Coronation for which she also had an entry. Glyfada from Ireland and Repel, a cosy winner last time, from France look interesting too.

5.35 King Edward VII Stakes

Mile and a half Group Two for three-year-old colts and geldings. A bit of a Derby consolation and a few of those who ran below expectation at Epsom may get out again today including the controversial Derby non-runner, Benventuto Cellini who got his hind leg stuck on a stall but still finished 10th. That is less than a fortnight ago and personally I would be looking elsewhere. It was all a bit too much of a rush to get Water To Wine to Epsom after his missed Chester with a temperature but he looks tailor-made for this. He is now two from two with an aggregate winning distance of 15 lengths having warmed up for this impressively on the all-weather.

6.10 Palace of Holyroodhouse Stakes

A five furlong sprint for three-year-olds. It is a very different course to Epsom but Gemma Tutty’s Call Margot had all the doors shut in her face at a critical point in the Dash on Derby day and but for that would surely have won. At Ascot, at least, there should be less in the way of traffic problems. The trainer had a second here before. That said, could Gold Digger be the one to break Saffie Osborne’s duck at the meeting? She certainly thinks so. Sixth in the Albany last year, Richard Spencer’s filly was a cosy winner at Windsor on her first start since.

News.title: World leaders urged to push through Pandemic Agreement
News.content:
Big pharma fears that by signing up to PABS it will be obliged to more formally recognise countries’ “genetic resources” – something that could impinge on their intellectual property rights and limit profits.

Countries fear that if they simply give away those resources, they will not receive the tests, vaccines and treatments made from them – something that happened during Covid-19 when developing countries were amongst the last to receive jabs.

“The PABS system rests on a simple, fair bargain: those who share dangerous pathogens quickly must be able to trust that the vaccines and treatments born from that sharing will reach their own people too”, says the letter to G7 leaders.

“Every one of us has a stake on both sides of it … This is not charity, and it is not only conscience…. A virus left to burn anywhere will, in time, find everyone,” it adds.

Citing research published in 2023, the letter says there is “close to a one in four chance of another pandemic within the coming decade”.

“Climate change, changing land use and evolving agriculture are redrawing the map of where dangerous pathogens emerge; the comfortable belief that outbreaks begin only in distant places is no longer true, and future hotspots may arise in or near your own countries,” it warns.

“At the same time, advances in biotechnology, matched unevenly by biosafety, raise the risk of accidental or deliberate release”.

It is unclear, and perhaps unlikely, that a truly global agreement on benefits sharing can be reached.

The US, like Argentina, has pulled out of the WHO and is not a party to the Pandemic Agreement. At the same time, the US is home to many of the world’s biggest pharmaceutical companies.

Nevertheless, an agreement between the remaining 192 member states of the WHO is possible and would represent a major step forward.

“Every month this annex stays unfinished is a month the world is less ready than it could be, and people are less safe than they deserve to be,” say Mr Lula da Silva and Dr Tedros.

“Finalising this Agreement, through a shared commitment to one another, is our collective promise to protect humanity”.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

Sports.title: Why England and all other World Cup rivals should be worried after Spain are humbled by Cape Verde
Sports.content:
SPAIN were completely stunned by Cape Verde in their World Cup opener on Monday.

The reigning European champions were held to a 0-0 draw by the tournament debutants.





But they still cannot be ruled out of contention for the trophy.

When La Roja last won the World Cup 16 years ago, they bounced back from an opening match defeat to Switzerland.

Gelson Fernandes scored the decisive goal on that occasion – coincidentally, he was born in Cape Verde.

Spain went on to win their remaining two group stage fixtures against Honduras and Chile before defeating Portugal 1-0 in the round-of-16.



After that came a 1-0 win over Paraguay in the quarter-finals and a 1-0 victory against Germany in the semi-finals.

Vicente del Bosque’s side then took on the Netherlands in the final and earned a 1-0 win thanks to a late goal from Andres Iniesta in added time.

Argentina found themselves in a similar position at the last World Cup in 2022.

The eventual champions suffered a shock opening match loss to Saudi Arabia in Qatar.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

After captain Lionel Messi broke the deadlock from the penalty spot, Saleh Al-Shehri and Salem Al-Dawsari scored in quick succession to fire Saudi Arabia to a 2-1 victory.

Argentina were able to put the loss behind them, however, and went on to beat Mexico and Poland in their other group stage fixtures.

The South American nation then enjoyed wins against Australia, the Netherlands and Croatia in the knockouts before their dramatic win on penalties against France in the final.

If anything, losing an opening World Cup match could actually be viewed as a good omen by some – especially because, on this occasion, three teams from most groups will qualify for the knockouts.



The European champions will know they are more than capable of bouncing back.

And if they can gain momentum quickly, it could be a huge warning for England and other rival nations.

Sports.title: Belgium 1 Egypt 1: Romelu Lukaku makes impact just 22 SECONDS after coming on to rescue point
Sports.content:
ROMELU LUKAKU’S instant impact snatched away Egypt’s first-ever World Cup victory.

The sheer presence of Belgium’s all-time top goalscorer forced a second-half own goal from Egypt as they had to settle for a point in Seattle.





Lukaku’s strength and speed off the bench changed the game and meant Premier League greats Mohamed Salah and Kevin De Bruyne had to share the spoils in the battle on the world stage.

Salah, who was celebrating his 34th birthday, and De Bruyne are both firmly in the twilight of their careers these days, with neither translating their club success to their national teams.

The days of the pair battling for Premier League titles are well and truly over, but this was a last-dance of sorts as they went head-to-head for a shot at football’s biggest prize.

Even with Belgium coming into the fixture as firm favourites, Egypt were playing without any fear.

That confidence can’t have come from their history in this competition, with the Pharaohs never winning a single World Cup game before.

But there was supreme confidence in the strike that opened the scoring.

Emam Ashour slapped home a stunning long-distance effort that left Belgium and Real Madrid stopper Thibaut Courtois helpless.

Ashour, who plays in Egypt’s top flight for Al-Ahly, wrapped his right boot around the ball to drill it past Courtois and into the bottom corner in the 20th minute.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

Fifa’s official stats put the goal down as a Salah assist, and it was, but even Egypt’s greatest ever player couldn’t take any of the credit away from Ashour, who had scored his first ever international goal in his 28th game for his country.

A hydration break soon followed the goal, stunting any momentum that Egypt could have gained and forced Hossam Hassan’s side into a low block for the remainder of the half, as they soaked up a red wave of pressure from Belgium.

Belgium weren’t exactly forcing the issue, with a lot of pedestrian football, and the threat of Jeremy Doku was largely nullified by right-back Mohamed Hany.

Egypt almost doubled their lead when Mostafa Ziko fizzed a low effort across the face of goal and forced a low save from Courtois.



The Red Devils ended the half without a shot on target, not least because Doku had sliced a golden opportunity over the crossbar from about 10 yards out.

The Belgians upped the ante in the second half, De Bruyne slapping the left upright with a free-kick in the 53rd minute and seeing another effort saved after an hour had passed.

But boss Rudi Garcia was still forced to look to the bench to add the missing spark in the 67th minute when he brought on Lukaku.

Lukaku, who has scored 90 goals for Belgium, took just 22 seconds to cause havoc as his run in behind the Egypt back line forced an own goal.



Thomas Meunier fired a cross into the area in search of the former Chelsea and Manchester United striker, but the outstretched foot of Hany intervened and poked the ball into the back of his own net.

The goal didn’t just end Belgium’s dry attacking in this game, but also a run of 292 minutes without a World Cup goal.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Belgium will feel they could have gone on to win the game, coming close with another Lukaku effort deep in the second half and forcing a number of impressive saves from Mostafa Shobeir.

But given the relative quality of the other sides in Group G, a point will probably be enough to help both sides progress come the end of the group stage.

Sports.title: Liverpool ‘set to bring back Darwin Nunez on free transfer’, sensational reports claim
Sports.content:
FORMER Liverpool man Darwin Nunez has been tipped for a sensational return to the club.

The Uruguayan forward only left Anfield last summer, joining Saudi Pro League outfit Al Hilal on a deal worth around £46million.





But according to football journalist Juan Pablo Romero, he could be set to link back up with his former side on a free transfer.

The Uruguay-based reporter claimed that a deal for the forward is all lined up.

They added that confirmation about the move would not arrive during the World Cup, where Nunez is competing for his nation, to allow him to keep his full concentration on the tournament.

Nunez’s time in the middle east took a sour turn after just months at the club following the arrival of legendary France forward Karim Benzema.

He was not included in the side’s league squad to accommodate for the new arrival, leaving him eligible to play only in continental competition.

His limbo at the club means he may well be available on a cut-price deal, or even be willing to walk away from his big-money contract, but reports of a return to Liverpool specifically come as quite the surprise.

The 26-year-old had appeared to burn some bridges at the club before his eventual departure.

His inconsistent form left him the target of mixed feelings from the fanbase in the North East.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

There were rumours of a tense relationship with now-sacked manager Arne Slot during their tenure together, with the boss having to shut down whispers of a training ground spat between the duo.

And he even appeared to lash out as his lack of playing time during his final months at the club, before deleting the offending social media post.

Slot has since departed the club, with Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola stepping in to replace the Dutchman.

Nunez has been linked to a number of Premier League sides given his experience in the division and his current club situation.

Both Newcastle and Chelsea have been named as potential suitors for the star if he is willing to give up on his £400,000-a-week wages.



But the links will still come as a shock U-turn so quickly after his acrimonious exit.

Sports.title: Anthony Gordon had just SIX Spanish lessons before England World Cup star turned heads at Barcelona unveiling
Sports.content:
ANTHONY GORDON took just six Spanish lessons before speaking the lingo in his Barcelona unveiling.

The England winger impressed with his foreign language skills after making the shock £70million move from Newcastle.





Gordon revealed: “It is difficult. People always see the end results.

“When you practise a little bit, it becomes a lot easier but it is really difficult. I’d had six lessons.

“I have had nine now because I have had a few here. I would not say I am intellectually smart.

“I always spoke a little bit of Spanish with my Spanish physio for this reason — but I’d had six lessons until the other day.”



Gordon, who has 18 Three Lions caps, is pushing to start against Croatia in Dallas on Wednesday after impressing against Costa Rica in a 3-0 warm-up victory in Orlando last Wednesday.

The former Everton star said: “I try to be direct. It’s what I am good at.

“I was blessed genetically in terms of pace, so it would be a waste not to use it.

“That is where I need to be a game-changer. I need to make sure I am effective in those situations.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

“This is my first World Cup and I cannot wait to hear the national anthem.

“The real stuff starts. It is exciting. We are creating memories, as we will never get this time back.”

Asked about playing under England manager Thomas Tuchel, Gordon said: “He is unique. He is an amazing person. He is very sarcastic and very funny once training has stopped.

“You can be yourself, which is not always the case with some managers.”

Gordon, 25, finds his zen each day by meditating.



The pacy winger says it is his secret to staying calm before every training session or match.

He said: ”I meditate every morning and it is purely to think about what I want to achieve through the day, in the session, in the game.

“It makes it easier for me to channel into my next decision.

“If I have a goal, every decision I make through the day, has to be headed towards that and it is easier to end up getting there.

“If I don’t do it, I feel I am all over the place. It is a bit of calm. Football is about letting things go.”

Gordon, who won the Under-21 Euros with England in 2023, added: “Whether you do bad or good. If I make a mistake, when I meditate, I make it easier to let it go and to be right in the moment.

“That moment could decide a game.”

Sports.title: Forgotten former Chelsea man switched allegiance from England before World Cup and will be key man for ex-Man Utd boss
Sports.content:
NIGERIAN parents, played for England at youth level and even eligible for France.

But now Carney Chukwuemeka is hoping to take Austria on a historic World Cup run.





They kick off their Group J campaign against Jordan in the early hours of Wednesday morning.

And Chukwuemeka, 22, will be desperate to make an impact in just his fourth cap after switching allegiance earlier this year.

The former Aston Villa and Chelsea midfielder played for the Young Lions from Under-16s through to U20s and won the 2022 U19s Euros but, with no senior England caps, opted to give himself a shot at representing his homeland.

He was born in Vienna but moved with his family, including older brother and fellow footballer Caleb, to Northampton when he was two.



Former Austria international Johnny Ertl told SunSport: “Chukwuemeka always said he has a strong connection to Vienna, because the first two years of his life he spent in Vienna.

“Also, his relation to David Alaba was important, with the Nigerian roots.

“Chukwuemeka had a great debut for Austria. He scored a cracking goal. It couldn’t get any better for him.

“It wasn’t the conventional route. Paul Wanner from Germany did the same as Chukwuemeka and also made his debut against Ghana.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

“It wasn’t a coincidence that Chukwuemeka switched before the World Cup.

“Over the last three years, the Austrian Football Federation has been in touch with him.

“It’s a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity for him to play at the cup, and to just present himself at the biggest stage.”



As Ertl referenced, Chukwuemeka is not the only man with Nigerian roots in Austria’s squad.

Real Madrid defender David Alaba’s dad is an Orege Yoruba prince from the western African nation.

The Austria captain, 33, and his deputy Marko Arnautovic, 37, have a combined 246 caps for the Burschen and could bring up their 250 milestone in the second Group J game against Argentina.

Ertl believes the veteran pair and young hotshots, under the guidance of former Manchester United temporary boss Ralf Rangnick, could go very deep into the tournament.

The ex-Crystal Palace and Portsmouth midfielder added: “After 28 years, Austria qualified for the World Cup. So, that means a lot for our country.



CLICK ON PIC FOR STAR’S PROFILE

“The round of 16 is achievable, the quarter-finals would be a success, and anything beyond that would be historic.

“We have Jordan in the first game. We must win. Full stop. That eases the pressure for the Argentina game because we are underdogs and then it’s make or break against Algeria. It’s as simple as that.

“Our key strength is the team spirit. We don’t have a really stand-out player.

“We have Alaba, but he’s coming back from an injury, but he’s very important. He’s Ralf Rangnick’s right-hand man.

“We have Marko Arnautovic who is the record goalscorer and still scoring. Whenever he plays for Austria, he looks like 27 not 37.



“Rangnick is not the only one who’s been associated with a terrible time at Manchester United.

“But I rate him highly as a human and as a man, because he’s a game changer.

“Austria was in the middle of nowhere as a football country before he went to Red Bull Salzburg [as director of football in 2012].

“He created the pathway for Austrian football to be successful in the future.

“As a manager, you need to be clear and authentic. These are the two attributes you need.

“He acts like a father figure for the players. He also demands a lot, don’t forget this, so it’s not easy to work under Ralf Rangnick.”

Sports.title: Six simple ways to survive World Cup chaos as late-night kick-offs bring wave of shattered school mornings and meltdowns
Sports.content:
IT was when I awoke from a 20-minute coma and saw it wasn’t even half-time that I realised this World Cup was going to be one hell of a ­logistical challenge.

England’s friendly with Costa Rica in Orlando last week wasn’t exactly a must-watch fixture but, kicking off at 10pm thanks to the wrong kind of hurricane, it sure as hell tested the eyelids.





Ten o’clock kick-offs are relatively early starts at this year’s tournament — which is being hosted by the US, Mexico and Canada — as all those hungover Scots who had to wait until nearly 4am on Sunday to see their team scrape a 1-0 victory over fellow minnows Haiti can attest.

I managed to get to the end of Brazil vs Morocco before the land of nod stamped my visa, so it wasn’t until my usual 3am call of nature that I caught up with Scotland’s scrappy opener.

Now, all these late nights are one thing for dozy dads like me to contend with, but for footie-mad kids, it is a whole different ball game.

A World Cup comes but once every four years so, of course, you want the whole family to enjoy as much of the joy — and disappointment — as they can.



But how do you juggle allowing kids to stay up until silly o’clock with getting up for school and them not immediately exploding into a full-blown tantrum that would make Joey Barton wince?

Well, in between matches (and naps) I have come up with an indispensable guide.

Just follow my six simple solutions and you (and your kids) will be all over this World Cup like Diego Maradona at Mexico ’86.

1. RIG THE SWEEPSTAKE



FIRST things first, you need to neutralise any additional incentives for your offspring to stay up late.

And that means making sure the kids only have teams in the family sweepstake that mostly play at sensible hours.

Yes, yes, I know you have probably already done the sweepstake, but let’s face it, everyone has got some stinkers in their hand so it is unlikely they will complain if you redo it.

Say you are doing it as you “want to make things interesting” by offering a small prize to the winner and so it is only fair if you start over. (Don’t tell them that the prize you have in mind is two tickets to the Empty The Dishwasher Club, else that will just spoil it.)

Next, when you pretend to randomly pick the teams out of mum’s holiday hat, ensure you give your kids as few late starters as possible.



So that means teams like Algeria — who play at 2, 3 and 4am — should be for the adults, while countries like Bosnia — all 8pm matches — should be for kids.

Capisce?

2. NO BOOZE UNTIL AN HOUR BEFORE THE GAME*

I KNOW, I know. What a killjoy, right?

But think about it.



Stick to your usual Thursday night Prem match drinking pace and you’ll be on the sauce by 6pm.

Unless you are the town’s Champion Beer Monster, five or six ales later it’s all over and you are off home for a kip or leaving the sofa to head up to bed. The day’s done.

Now imagine having to sit there for another TWO games, which is exactly what you may be planning tonight.

There’s France v Senegal starting at 8pm, then Iraq v Norway at 11pm followed by the Argies taking on Algeria at 2am.

The 5am Austria vs Jordan clash will just have to go whistle.



Stick to your usual Thursday mid-match drinking pace and you’ll be getting your stomach pumped by the time Messi nets his first.

And good luck getting yourself — or indeed anyone — out of bed in time for work/school with half a case of San Miguel still coursing through your veins.

Moderation is the key here.

* Unless it is England, in which case fill your boots!

3. NO SUGARY CRAP



EVEN if you are watching Portugal v Uzbekistan at 6pm and you have only just finished your fish fingers, you are going to need to load up on snacks.

The kids will want them and, be honest, so will you.

Now the key thing here is to skip the sugary stuff.

Haribo, Tony’s Chocolonely, a handful of Celebrations, it has all got to go. It is a scientific fact that a single Tangfastic given to a child during a football match will make them to go absolutely berserk.

And the sugar crash they get after will make the hangover you had after nailing 16 pints during last year’s Women’s Euros final look like, er, child’s play.



By the time you traipse off to bed you are unlikely to be bothered about cleaning all that sherbet off your teeth. So serve only crisps, nuts and those little cheesy nibbles you get in Poundland that look like playing card symbols.

You could even make it interesting by serving savoury snacks local to the country you are watching.

Just ask your local Tesco Metro for some traditional Congolese kamundele next time you’re in.

4. PYJAMAS ON FOR EVERY MATCH

I DON’T care if they are 15 now and “this is just embarrassing Daaaaaaad” but anyone under 18 must be ready for bed before any match kicks off.



And I mean ANY match — even Thursday’s Czech Republic v South Africa clash, which starst at 5pm. Rules are rules.

It will be much easier to cart them off to bed when they inevitably fall asleep during the penalty stages.

If you are one of those “creative” parents, you could make it fun by insisting the little cherubs wear PJs that best match the colours of the shirt worn by the team they want to win.

And you can get into your pyjamas too, saving yourself some valuable time in the early hours, thus giving you no excuse to not brush your teeth (again).

5. NO SLEEPOVERS ON A SCHOOL NIGHT



IT will be very tempting to have friends over to stay so your collective kids can entertain themselves while you drink and marvel at the sheer pluckiness of Curacao, the smallest nation to ever reach the World Cup.

This might work well at weekends when no one has to get up, but on weekdays you are asking for trouble.

Think how you are going to get everyone off to school or work on time when you have to rustle up a dozen bacon sandwiches and make small talk about what they are all doing this summer holiday.

And just having a kids-only sleepover is also a no-no.

No doubt your teen has already pestered you to have “just a few of my mates who I play Fifa with” round. Resist.



You don’t know all those weird voices that come out of your son’s PS5.

Some of them are spotty weirdos who have no interest in watching the game — they just want to steal your stash of chilled beers.

6. WAKE THE KIDS UP FOR ALL THE GAMES EVEN 4AM ONES

BE honest, you don’t really want to watch the vast majority of those early-hours matches.

Crawling out of your scratcher to watch Paraguay v Turkey at 4am sounded like great larks when you boasted about doing it in the pub, but the reality of it will hit hard.



Imagine getting up for the first Ryanair flight to Magaluf, but instead of a golden beach at the end, you get a 0-0 draw between Iran and New Zealand.

Despite your best efforts with the sweepstake and warning your kids that early-morning matches will leave them exhausted, they of course won’t listen and will INSIST on being allowed to watch them.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

So your best bet is to allow it. Install a clock in their rooms and set the alarm sound to the “donkey with croup” setting.

After a few nights of this ear-splitting intrusion they will never want to wake up for a football match again.

Sports.title: SWAT team rushes to armed standoff just mile from England World Cup stadium as suspect arrested
Sports.content:
A SWAT team and a host of armed police yesterday responded to an incident a mile from where England’s first match will be played.

An officer at the scene described it as “pretty serious”, with a weapon brandished by a suspect.





The incident in Arlington, Texas, was near the AT&T Stadium where England play Croatia tomorrow.

Police said it was a domestic dispute between two people, adding: “The female was barricaded in the home with additional occupants. No injuries were reported.

“The report shows that a weapon was produced but no injuries were reported.

“The suspect is now in custody and the investigation is ongoing.”

There is no indication the incident was connected to the World Cup or posed any threat to the tournament or its venues.

A referee Thomas Tuchel once labelled “terrible” and gave a “1/10” rating will be in charge of England’s World Cup opener against Croatia.

Clement Turpin, voted the world’s best ref in 2025, has been appointed by Fifa to officiate the Group L clash in Dallas on Wednesday.

It is the first game the 44-year-old will officiate at this tournament in his third World Cup overall, having worked at Russia 2018 and Qatar four years ago.



Frenchman Turpin knows both sides well, having already officiated England five times and Croatia four.

The standout result of that quintet of Three Lions matches was the humiliating 4-0 home defeat to Hungary in the Nations League four years ago.

Though England did win three of the others – beating Slovakia 2-1 in a 2018 World Cup qualifier, Switzerland 1-0 in a friendly the same year and Italy 3-1 in a Euro qualifier three years ago.



The most recent England fixture he officiated was the dismal 0-0 draw against Slovenia at Euro 2024.

And Tuchel might not be too happy to see him.

In 2023 he fumed at Turpin after being sent off when Bayern Munich boss in a Champions League quarter-final loss to Manchester City.

German Tuchel was shown two yellow cards on the touchline by Turpin and tore into him after the match.

Sports.title: World Cup LIVE: Egypt denied first win vs Belgium as FIFA Iran ban upheld
Sports.content:
10,000 England fans heading to Dallas for Croatia match

A 10,000-strong army of England fans is heading to Dallas to see our World Cup opener against Croatia. Superfan Robert Didd has attended every single England home game since 1986, setting a record of 222 consecutive games from 1987 to 2007. He has spent around £500,000 following his country but does not regret a penny.

My first game was in October 1986, and I have been to every single home game in 40 years. In the 90s, I calculated that I had spent around £100,000 following England, but it must be about £500,000 now. I would have a bigger house and a few extra bedrooms. But I have been to 76 countries. It is like being an explorer, travelling the world you see on TV or read about in a book.

He was pictured at an early game, aged 16, with his Mitcham/Chelsea England flag. He has kept match tickets and memorabilia from a lifetime of following the national side. His 'fear' is of missing out if England win the World Cup.

Civil servant Garford, 64, of London, is at his 10th World Cup, spending around £12,000 on the trip. Garford is heading to Dallas and from there will take a Greyhound bus to Boston, a journey of 40 hours.

It is £135 with three changes, but it will be a real experience and give me time to think and see parts of America that I would never have seen otherwise. You leave at 3.15am, which may not be very comfortable, but I am going to Nashville and New York before Boston, and through Memphis, Jackson, Knoxville, and Charlottesville. That is what you will remember, the places and the people."

England Supporters' Association leads the Fans' Embassy service in the US and did a four-day road trip from Florida to Dallas via Tallahassee, Florida, Mobile, Alabama, and Natchez, Mississippi. A Newcastle United fan, he told of a 'church every half mile' in Louisiana and rolling countryside reminiscent of his native Northumberland.

The country roads were like the A1 when it goes into single file in North Northumberland. It was old school America. The only thing missing was the Johnny Cash soundtrack. It is worth it when you get here, as the Dallas stadium is absolutely magnificent. I think the number of England supporters here, when you consider the financial challenges, is just incredible and a real credit to them."

He stressed the need to carry water because of the extreme heat forecast for the 3pm kick-off time, with temperatures expected to reach 32-33 °C, around 90F. The match is set to be played under the roof at the stadium to make it cooler for players and fans.

Chris Thomas, 40, originally from Leeds, is leaving at 3am tomorrow (Wednesday) from Kansas City to get to the game in time for kick-off. Chris, who sells traditional British pies with a street food firm called 'Brit Boy', now living in Kansas City, is with his best friend, Sam Bannister, also from Leeds, and Kye Marty, another ex-pat, and his American wife, Sundy.

The stadium is about 45 minutes outside the city, so we will be driving and using taxis and public transport when we get there. Otherwise, the costs can be horrific. It is a mixture of excitement and trepidation now. I just hope England give it a good go."

Exeter City fan George Smith, a finance worker who now lives in San Diego, California, is travelling to the England group games with Three Lions supporters based in Spain, Scandinavia and Australia. George, 42, is taking his son Charlie, 11, to the England games with him. He also plans to take his Mexican-born wife, Monica, to the famous Azteca stadium if England face her native country in the Round of 16.

In total, George has spent around $7,000 dollars (£5,178) on tickets for himself and his family. But the bill may rise to £12,000 depending on how far England progress.

Sports.title: Paul Pogba issues Man Utd Premier League title prediction under Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Paul Pogba issues Man Utd Premier League title prediction under Michael Carrick

Michael Carrick was handed the permanent Manchester United head coach role in the summer after impressing as interim boss and former teammate Paul Pogba believes he could lead the Red Devils to the Premier League title

View 2 Images Paul Pogba has given his take on Man United (Image: Getty Images)

Paul Pogba believes Manchester United will end their Premier League title drought under Michael Carrick. The former United midfielder impressed as interim boss last term as he led the club back into the Champions League.

‌



He was consequently handed the role on a permanent basis. The Red Devils are already determined to back Carrick in the transfer market, with moves for Ederson, as well as another central midfielder, on the way.

‌



And Pogba believes those signings could potentially help the club to end their 13-year wait for a Premier League title. Asked by talkSPORT if the club could claim the crown under former teammate Carrick, the Frenchman replied: “Yes.

‌



“I think Manchester United will win in the next years, they’re going to be champions of the Premier League. If Arsenal can be champions then Manchester United will definitely be champion.

Marcus Rashford's thoughts on Barcelona transfer after Hansi Flick reaches out to Man Utd star READ MORE :

Man Utd take Mateus Fernandes transfer gamble as West Ham star tells bosses he wants move READ MORE :

“It’s a big statement. No disrespect but I believe they will. In the next five years they’re going to win. Maybe I went a bit far, I will say in the next three years. In my opinion I think they can make it.”

Pogba, 33, had two spells at United during his playing career. He was initially at Old Trafford between 2009 and 2012 but left for Juventus after finding opportunities limited.

‌



United re-signed the midfielder for a world record £88m in 2016 and he went on to score 39 goals in 226 appearances but failed to hit the heights expected of him before returning to Juventus for nothing.

View 2 Images Pogba has backed Carrick to help United to the Premier League crown (Image: Getty Images)

Pogba was banned in February 2024 for a failed drugs test but saw that ban reduced. He has since represented Ligue 1 side Monaco. His United prediction comes just days after he tipped France to win another World Cup, having claimed the current side are better than the one he helped to the title in 2018.

‌



Speaking to ESPN, Pogba said: "Yeah. I think everybody sees them as favourites. They have to [be]. They have probably the best players in the world.

"But obviously, that is not enough to win a World Cup, and there is more pressure on them," he continued, adding that "they have to keep the standard as high as possible."

He added: "For me, as players -- talent and everything -- I think they're better than us. Yeah, I think they're better than us. But then, obviously, hopefully, that will make them win the World Cup."

Sports.title: John Stones using Pep Guardiola frustration as England ace talks up World Cup form
Sports.content:
John Stones using Pep Guardiola frustration as England ace talks up World Cup form

John Stones has headed to the World Cup off the back of a frustrating final season at Manchester City - but believes he's primed to make an impact with England

View 2 Images John Stones insists he's in prime condition ahead of the World Cup

John Stones has revealed he has “never felt better” going into a tournament - and is determined to prove Pep Guardiola wrong.

‌



Stones made just five starts in the Premier League last season and that must make his inclusion in the World Cup squad a major gamble by Thomas Tuchel.

‌



But Stones, 32, was clearly frustrated at his lack of minutes in Guardiola’s final season in charge at Manchester City. That has given Stones an extra edge for this World Cup because he is determined to prove a point after his season of frustration.

‌



England defender Stones, who is now a free agent after his contract expired, said: “I was fit enough 100 per cent, it comes down to various things, the manager (Guardiola) and that’s something I can’t control and I think it’s always difficult to pick an XI and I say to this to him.

Ange Postecoglou picks out the worst thing about managing England at the World Cup READ MORE :

Rodri takes swipe at Cape Verde tactics after Spain suffered World Cup embarrassment READ MORE :

“He knows how much I wanted to play, how much I wanted to be there and you can look at it in so many ways. I think I feel as good as I’ve ever been before a tournament. Yeah, ready, ready to go, feel great, feel sharp and feel fresh and excited for it.”

Stones is on 79 caps and is already dreaming of reaching the 100 mark but also says he has a strong belief that England get over the line and go one step further after near misses.

‌



He added to ITV : “I’d love to. It’s always been my dream. I set a target of 50 and around that time, I never thought I’d play for England around 39 or 41 and I was stuck.

View 2 Images The defender has just left Man City, but was frustrated by his lack of minutes

"I thought that was it. I’ll stay on definitely. I feel too good and have too much to give and too much competitive within me and for my country.

‌



“I always believed we would win and that belief has to be a belief. It can’t be a hope. We all hope for good things to happen but when you have a belief it’s different. I’ve said from March and qualifying that we have that belief and we should feel that and look back on that.

“It’s difficult to put into words, if you’d said that to me as a kid that I’d get to those points in my career - especially in an England shirt - I feel immense pride but something is missing.”

Sports.title: Bukayo Saka ready to take World Cup 'gamble' in huge boost to England's chances
Sports.content:
Bukayo Saka ready to take World Cup 'gamble' in huge boost to England's chances

Arsenal and England forward Bukayo Saka is going into the tournament still suffering with an Achilles issue, but he is determined to not let it impact his World Cup

View 2 Images Bukayo Saka is battling to be fit for England's opener vs Croatia

Bukayo Saka has insisted he is ready to “gamble” on his fitness for England’s World Cup chances.

‌



Arsenal winger Saka, who is set to win his 50th cap against Croatia in their Group opener on Wednesday, has been struggling with an Achilles issue.

‌



It ruled Saka out of England’s March camp and he had to push himself through the pain barrier for Arsenal’s title run-in which cast a major doubt over his fitness for this summer. But Saka is determined to start which will give Thomas Tuchel a huge boost for England’s World Cup campaign.

‌



Saka, 24, said: “As players, it’s the biggest gamble, especially if you’re not feeling your sharpest. You have the choice whether you don’t play or you put yourself out there knowing people are going to judge you the same.

England's World Cup kit to look different to rivals as FIFA confirm late change READ MORE :

“I’m happy to take the gamble. It paid off, I’d say. I’m going to continue doing that. At the end of the day, people don’t really care how you’re feeling, they expect you to deliver. But I am feeling a lot better than I did in March and I’m ready to go.

“The main focus right now is winning the World Cup. And being my best version of myself for the team.”

‌



Saka was hugely influential in helping Arsenal win their first title in 22 years and also says that winning feeling has boosted his confidence.

He said: “Knowing what it takes to win is important and it gives you more belief. It gives you more confidence and freedom.

View 2 Images Bukayo Saka is happy to gamble on his fitness in a major boost to Thomas Tuchel (Image: Eddie Keogh/The FA via Getty Images)

‌



“When you have that success and you taste it, you want to do it again, and you can go two ways, but when I speak for myself, I'd say it's definitely feeling that I want to do it again and it gives me even more hunger.”

England boss Tuchel has said that Saka will not be able to start and finish every game but the Arsenal winger says he is happy to share the role with club teammate Noni Madueke.

Saka, who is also relishing the chance to reach 50 caps, added: “Noni is like my brother and we enjoy competing and playing together. Not many players have done that, especially so young. So it's proud for me.”

Sports.title: Rodri takes swipe at Cape Verde tactics after Spain suffered World Cup embarrassment
Sports.content:
Rodri takes swipe at Cape Verde tactics after Spain suffered World Cup embarrassment

Spain were unable to find a way past Cape Verde in their World Cup opener as Rodri took aim at their negative tactics in the goalless draw

View 2 Images Rodri didn't shy away from bemoaning Cape Verde's negative tactics

Rodri has taken aim at the tactics of Cape Verde after they held Spain to an incredible draw with the midfielder claiming they "don't get past midfield".

‌



The Euro 2024 winners came into the tournament as favourites, but were stunned by the World Cup minnows, who secured a goalless draw. They celebrated it like a win at full-time as the nation, with half a million people, managed to hold the international powerhouse.

‌



Spain by no means peppered the Cape Verde goal as they struggled to turn their possession into clear cut chances. Lamine Yamal was left on the bench following a injury hit period, but even his appearance on 70 minutes couldn't inspire Spain to a win in their opening game.

‌



Rodri is well accustomed to playing in teams that dominate games and have to deal with low blocks. The Manchester City talisman deals with it often in the Premier League, but on this occasion his Spanish side lack the potency in the box.

Ange Postecoglou picks out the worst thing about managing England at the World Cup READ MORE :

He told La 1: "It wasn’t meant to be. There’s little to complain about. We knew it was a game that required patience. They sat back and they dropped back very quickly. We couldn’t put it in. We created chances, but couldn’t finish. The positive thing is that they barely created anything against us. We need to improve our finishing."

‌



When quizzed on the tactics of Cape Verde the midfielder fired a dig, but equally confessed it was on Spain to be more clinical in front of goal. "That’s how they play. They don’t get past midfield," he added. "It’s a matter of improving our finishing."

View 2 Images Spain failed to find the net against the World Cup minnows

Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, who was the hero, was pictured in tears in the aftermath before he was handed the Player of the Match award.

‌



"It was a great match," he said. "We worked incredibly hard for this moment and this dream. We are very proud. We knew it wasn’t going to be easy."

Spain had 74 percent of the ball and 27 attempts on goal but still couldn't breach the Cape Verde goal. They threw on the likes of Yamal, Nico Williams and Dani Olmo in an effort to find a winning goal, but ultimately fell short.

The European champions will face Saudi Arabia next before rounding out their group campaign against Uruguay.

Sports.title: FIFA's Iran ban decision upheld in emergency World Cup meeting hours before New Zealand match
Sports.content:
FIFA's Iran ban decision upheld in emergency World Cup meeting hours before New Zealand match

A last-minute meeting took place in Los Angeles just before Iran's World Cup opener vs New Zealand

View 2 Images FIFA's ban on Iran's 'pre-revolutionary' flag has been upheld (Image: Henry NICHOLLS / AFP via Getty Images)

FIFA's ban on pre-revolutionary Iran flags during the World Cup tournament will remain following a late meeting just hours before the nation's tournament opener. Iran take on New Zealand at 2am BST on Tuesday morning.

‌



It seems that the flag in question will not be allowed to be seen. It was banned by FIFA, but was the subject of a lawsuit filed by an Iran fan intending to attend the game.

‌



The flag is similar to the official flag but also features a lion and sun motif in the middle. It's associated with the previous regime, which was overthrown in 1979.

‌



Lee Dixon fights back tears during ITV commentary after massive World Cup shock READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The Athletic reports that the case was heard on Monday morning in Los Angeles. Judge Curtis A. Kin ruled that the ban will stand.

“Free speech is incredibly important, it is sacred, a bedrock of our society, but it is not without limitation, such as private actor, on private property, and as shown by previous cases, regulating in reasonable way. I deny the application," he said.

‌



He added: “There may be harm to some 2,500 staff members who have to deal with safety protocols,”

"It is a tremendous burden to change a long-standing stadium protocol for a massive event in a period of hours. It is hard to see how FIFA could make a change at one stadium and not the rest.”

When asked by The Athletic if the flag would be banned, the organisation responded with: “Any materials, including but not limited to banners, flags, fliers, apparel and other paraphernalia, that are of a political, offensive and/or discriminatory nature, containing wording, symbols or any other attributes aimed at discrimination of any kind against a country, private person or group on account of race, skin colour, ethnicity, national or social origin, gender identity and expression, disability, language, religion, political opinion or any other opinion, birth, wealth or any other status, sexual orientation or on any other grounds."

‌



View 2 Images Demonstrators outside the hotel where the Iran national football team is staying (pictured on Sunday) (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



Iran take on New Zealand at the SoFi Stadium in California on Tuesday. In their second Group G match they face Belgium on June 31, with their third group game against Egypt on June 26.

The nation's participation in the tournament was in doubt due to the war between Iran and the United States. There has been an agreement to end the war.

There has however been threats that the nation's national anthem will be targeted by protests from activists. Speaking ahead of the game, head coach Amir Ghalenoei said that players will pay no attention to background noise.

"We don't pay attention to any of the hype and anything that goes on around us," he said, before adding: "We are not political people... football is separate from politics."
